title: Run a Real AI Model on Your Own Laptop (Free, Offline) [stock footage version]

shots.text: You don't need a data center to run a capable AI model. You need the laptop you already own.
Open AI models now run fully offline. No subscription, and your data never leaves your machine.

visual.query: person typing on laptop at night

shots.text: You need three things. The right tool, the right model size, and enough memory.

visual.query: hands typing on laptop keyboard close up

shots.text: Start with the tool. Ollama and LM Studio are both free, and they handle the hard parts for you.

visual.query: software developer computer screen close up

shots.text: With Ollama, one command downloads a model and starts a chat, right in your terminal.

visual.query: programmer terminal code on screen dark

shots.text: Prefer buttons over commands? LM Studio gives you a chat window, much like the apps you already use.
Next, pick the right model size. Size is measured in billions of parameters.
Bigger models are smarter, but they are also slower and hungrier for memory.

visual.query: abstract glowing neural network nodes, cinematic blue light

shots.text: A seven or eight billion parameter model, compressed to four bits, needs about five gigabytes of memory.
That fits comfortably on most laptops with sixteen gigabytes of RAM.
That compression is called quantization. It shrinks the model, with only a small loss in quality.
Finally, memory. On a Mac with Apple silicon, the GPU shares system memory, which helps a lot.
On Windows or Linux, a graphics card with its own video memory makes answers much faster.
No graphics card? It still works on the processor. Answers just arrive more slowly.
So why bother? Privacy, for one. Your notes and your code stay on your own disk.

visual.query: padlock over a laptop screen, dark moody cinematic lighting

shots.text: It also works with no internet at all. On a plane, or anywhere with bad Wi-Fi.
My advice? Start with a small model, check that it is fast enough, then try a bigger one.

visual.query: person thinking at desk with laptop

shots.text: Which model would you try first? Tell me in the comments, and subscribe for more practical AI guides.
